rationale: Multisource CMDB (CMDB 360) records each data source's reported value per attribute and shows the reconciled authoritative value, giving transparency into where data came from and why a value won.

distractor_notes.B: Coalesce matches import records; it doesn't track per-source values.
distractor_notes.C: UI policies change form behavior.
distractor_notes.D: Watch lists handle notifications.

subdomain: CMDB Data Manager and CI lifecycle
stem: An organization wants automated handling of CI lifecycle stages, like retiring and eventually deleting CIs that are no longer in the environment. Which tool manages this policy-driven lifecycle?

options.text: CMDB Data Manager
A transform map
A catalog UI policy
The MID Server

rationale: CMDB Data Manager applies policies across the CI lifecycle — for example, marking absent CIs for retirement and later cleanup — so stale data doesn't accumulate. It's a governance tool for lifecycle hygiene.

distractor_notes.B: Transform maps move imported data; they don't run lifecycle policies.
distractor_notes.C: Catalog UI policies control catalog variables.
distractor_notes.D: The MID Server is a connectivity bridge.

stem: Leadership wants new CIs blocked or flagged when required attributes are missing at creation. Which governance mechanism enforces such data-quality rules?

options.text: CMDB data policies / required-attribute rules
A coalesce field
A favorite
A scheduled report

rationale: CMDB policies (including required-attribute and data-quality rules) enforce standards on CI data so incomplete records are caught at the source. This is core to keeping completeness high.

distractor_notes.B: Coalesce matches records on import; it doesn't enforce required attributes.
distractor_notes.C: Favorites are shortcuts.
distractor_notes.D: A scheduled report measures but doesn't enforce.

stem: A team plans to load CIs through Discovery, a Service Graph Connector, and an import set. They worry each path needs its own duplicate-prevention logic. What's true about IRE?

options.text: IRE centrally identifies and reconciles CIs no matter which ingestion path is used
IRE only runs for Discovery data
Each ingestion path must implement its own matching
IRE only runs during nightly maintenance

rationale: IRE is the single, central point that identifies and reconciles CMDB writes from any source — Discovery, Service Graph Connectors, ETL, import, or API. That's why duplicate-prevention logic doesn't need to be rebuilt per path.

distractor_notes.B: IRE governs all ingestion paths, not just Discovery.
distractor_notes.C: Centralizing matching in IRE is exactly what avoids per-path logic.
distractor_notes.D: IRE runs as data is written, not only on a nightly schedule.

stem: You want to scope a health dashboard and remediation effort to just the CIs supporting a particular business unit. Which feature lets you define that subset of CIs?

options.text: CMDB groups
A coalesce field
A watch list
An update set

rationale: CMDB groups define a saved set of CIs (by query) that you can target for health scoring, dashboards, and remediation — useful for focusing on one business unit or service.

distractor_notes.B: Coalesce is an import-matching concept.
distractor_notes.C: Watch lists handle notifications.
distractor_notes.D: Update sets move configuration.

stem: Which TWO responsibilities belong to the Identification and Reconciliation Engine?

options.text: Identifying whether incoming data matches an existing CI
Reconciling which source is authoritative for an attribute
Rendering the Service Portal homepage
Sending SLA breach emails

rationale: IRE's two core jobs are identification (match incoming data to the right CI) and reconciliation (decide which source's value is authoritative). Portal rendering and SLA emails are unrelated platform features.

distractor_notes.C: The Service Portal is a separate end-user interface.
distractor_notes.D: SLA notifications are part of service-level management, not IRE.

stem: Which TWO are sound CMDB governance practices?

options.text: Use reconciliation rules to define authoritative sources per attribute
Run data certification so owners periodically verify CI accuracy
Let every integration overwrite any attribute freely
Skip identification rules to speed up ingestion

rationale: Defining authoritative sources via reconciliation rules and running data certification are core governance practices that protect data quality. Letting everything overwrite freely or skipping identification invites duplicates and bad data.

distractor_notes.C: Unrestricted overwrites destroy data integrity; that's what reconciliation prevents.
distractor_notes.D: Skipping identification rules causes duplicate CIs.
